Palm Hills physical page 1 reports rounded contract sales of EGP182 billion and rounded collections of EGP26 billion. The selected statement on physical page 4 reports recognized revenue of EGP25,549,856 thousand, exactly EGP25.549856 billion at its printed precision. Conventional direct rounding to one decimal billion gives EGP25.5 billion; the narrative's EGP25.6 billion is an inconsistent rounded headline, potentially reflecting intermediate rounding, but the cause is not established. Use the selected statement number without silently replacing it or calling the discrepancy a restatement.

Developer contract sales represent bookings across future delivery/recognition periods, revenue follows the applicable recognition policy, and collections include cash from old receivables as well as new sales. Adding these measures double-counts overlapping activity and confuses stocks of commitments with accounting and cash flows. The EGP225 billion undelivered backlog supports prospective activity, but is neither immediately earned revenue nor cash. EGP26 billion collections exceeding current-period revenue is not proof of exceptional profit conversion: selected operating cash flow is only EGP748.335 million after operating payments and working capital. Construction spending of EGP10.5 billion indicates continuing delivery obligations. Need cancellation rates, installment schedules, recognition policy, construction commitments and collection aging. Decision: recognize historical commercial momentum while investigating conversion and commitments; no current valuation or investment clearance follows from these historical rounded highlights.
